page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 architecture, driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of computational capability. In CPU-focused evaluations, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1100.49 and a multi-core score of 2931.93, both categorized as weak. Geekbench testing further highlights these limitations, with a single-core score of 918.0 and a multi-core score of 1990.0, placing its raw processing power in the bottom 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth tests show a similar trend, with uncached large-block read speeds of 20.19 GB/sec and write speeds of 18.14 GB/sec, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-intensive operations despite the generous capacity.

From a workload perspective, the ecs.se1.xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive applications that do not require high-performance compute or rapid local disk I/O. Examples include caching layers such as Redis, where it achieved 2.87 million SET operations per second, or lightweight database operations. However, its poor performance in single-threaded compression, image processing, and web serving suggests it is less optimal for high-traffic web servers or intensive data compilation tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates modest performance, with weak CPU and memory bandwidth results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1990.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 3629.17. Consequently, this instance is best utilized for memory-intensive workloads with low compute demands, such as in-memory caching with Redis or basic database operations, rather than high-throughput web serving or intensive computational tasks.
